title: Thyrotoxicosis: clinical features and Graves disease
sec: Thyrotoxicosis: clinical features and Graves disease · p910
guide: Map constitutional, neurological, cardiovascular and gastrointestinal features of thyrotoxicosis. Recognise infiltrative ophthalmopathy, pretibial myxoedema and acropachy as Graves-specific.

title: Graves eye signs, scoring and diagnosis
sec: Graves eye signs, scoring and diagnosis · p911
guide: Use activity and severity scoring to classify Graves ophthalmopathy. Smoking cessation and steroid cover for radioiodine are central to management; TRAb positivity separates Graves from most mimics.

title: Thionamides, RAI and surgical management of thyrotoxicosis
sec: Thionamides, RAI and surgical management of thyrotoxicosis · p912
guide: Methimazole is preferred in non-pregnant adults; PTU is reserved for T1 pregnancy and thyroid storm. RAI is definitive but avoided in active ophthalmopathy; total thyroidectomy is preferred in large goitres and pregnancy.

title: Thyroid storm, neonatal thyrotoxicosis, surgery complications
sec: Thyroid storm, neonatal thyrotoxicosis, surgery complications · p913
guide: Burch-Wartofsky ≥ 45 suggests thyroid storm; treat with thionamide first, iodine after ≥1 h, beta-blocker and hydrocortisone. Neonatal thyrotoxicosis from transplacental TRAb is treated with thionamide plus beta-blocker.

title: Thyroiditis classification
guide: Distinguish Hashimoto, subacute (de Quervain), postpartum and acute suppurative thyroiditis by pain, ESR, antibodies and uptake. NSAID and beta-blocker treat subacute; antibiotics and drainage treat acute suppurative.

title: Subacute and postpartum thyroiditis course
sec: Subacute and postpartum thyroiditis course · p915
guide: Subacute and postpartum thyroiditis follow a biphasic course with eventual recovery in most patients. NSAIDs ease pain; levothyroxine covers the hypothyroid phase; permanent hypothyroidism develops in a minority.

title: Amiodarone thyroid disease and drug-induced thyroiditis
sec: Amiodarone thyroid disease and drug-induced thyroiditis · p916
guide: Type 1 amiodarone thyrotoxicosis is iodine-induced (treated with thionamides); Type 2 is destructive (treated with steroids). Lithium, IFN-α and ICIs each have characteristic thyroid signatures worth memorising.
